messages:
maria: heads-up — since the RBAC push earlier today, we’re seeing intermittent mTLS handshakes fail between eu-west proxies and apac ingest. errors show KMS decrypt denied in eu-west only.
maria: sample log: `tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate` then `kms:Decrypt AccessDenied for role proxy-keystore-eu`.
aj: is the keystore service account the one changed in the RBAC change? which pr rolled? :thinking:
maria: PR #5143 — removed broad kms:Decrypt on `infra-proxies` and added tighter role bindings, per least-privs. I can paste the diff:
```
- roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter: members: [group:infra-proxies@redwood.com]
+ roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter: members: [serviceAccount:proxy-keystore-eu@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com]
```
maria: the odd bit: apac and us regions are fine; only eu-west shows AccessDenied in the audit logs when the proxy attempts to unwrap session keys.
devin: can you paste the exact audit log entry (proto payload) and the service identity used by the proxy process? sometimes the pod uses a node service account via workload identity mapping.
kevin: audit log snippet: `principal=system:serviceaccount:proxy:proxy-keystore`, `resource=kmsKey/projects/redwood/locations/europe-west1/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/proxy` , `status=PERMISSION_DENIED`, `methodName=cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.asymmetricDecrypt`.
sofia: @maria can you confirm workload identity mapping for eu cluster? iirc we recently rotated node pool and might have lost annotation on node pool metadata.
maria: checking — eu nodes show annotation `iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account=proxy-keystore-eu@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` on some nodes but not all. looks like rollout created a mix.
aj: that would explain intermittent failures (some pods scheduled on nodes without proper mapping). quick check: `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.metadata.annotations}\n' | grep proxy-keystore`.
maria: ran that — 6/10 nodes missing mapping. rolling update earlier may not have reapplied node annotation.
kevin: workaround: add temporary permission back to the group until we fix node annotations. but that weakens least-priv model. alternative: reattach correct SA to nodes and cordon+drain.
devin: also check KMS key policy for region restrictions. is key restricted to eu-west callers? sometimes we lock `condition` on caller's `location` attribute.
sofia: good call. policy shows a binding with condition `request.time < timestamp('2026-04-01T00:00:00Z')` for the old group. no geo condition. not the blocker.
sec-bot: alert created: incident-ktls-2026-03-21; linked runbook `keystore-workflow`. suggested next steps: revert permissive binding OR fix node annotations + rolling drain.
maria: plan of action proposed: (1) add back kms:Decrypt to `infra-proxies` group for eu as hotfix (rollback scope-limited), (2) patch node pool automation to reapply annotations and cordon/drain in controlled batch, (3) re-run terraform for GKE node-pool IAM binding, (4) remove temp permission and validate via audit logs.
aj: for step 1 use least blast radius: attach to group `infra-proxies-eu` not org-wide. command:
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding proxy --location=europe-west1 --keyring=keystore --member=group:infra-proxies-eu@redwood.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```
maria: I'll hold on step 1 until we schedule a 15-min maintenance window. prefer draining nodes quickly.
devin: double-check time skew across eu nodes too — TLS failures sometimes from cert validity checks if node clocks drift.
sofia: good call — `chronyc tracking` shows one node ~5m drift; should be <5s. that could cause some cert validation to fail.
maria: ok we have two orthogonal issues: node annotation mismatch (scheduling leads to wrong SA) + at least one node with bad clock. both can cause the intermittent AccessDenied/TLS errors.
kevin: after we fix, monitor audit logs for `methodName=cloudkms.*Decrypt` and mTLS handshake success rate. set an alert if failure rate >1% in 10m.
sec-bot: action items assigned: maria -> node patch + coord maintenance, aj -> prepare terraform and gcloud rollback command, devin -> time-sync remediation playbook, kevin -> monitor dashboards and alert thresholds.
maria: thanks all — starting node patch now. will update thread once first 3 nodes drained and re-annotated.
